paragraphs.text: Y562 is a named export recipe from the Yunnan Tea Import and Export Company, sold under Jixing, its export brand, whose name means fortune. In the old coding the Y marks the company, and the number stands for leaf grade and factory. Grade five to six points to fine, tender leaf, unlike the coarse ripe bricks made in the same years.

This [ripe pu’er](shou:definition) dates from 1993, twenty years after Yunnan’s state factories brought [wet piling](shou:wet-piling) into production. It was kept loose in a box rather than pressed into a cake, and it has spent the years since around 1993 in dry storage in Hong Kong. At thirty-three years it sits well within what the trade counts as [aged ripe pu’er](shou:age-aged), and that dry storage has shaped it as much as the years have.

brewing.text: Ripe pu’er takes boiling water and forgives a heavy hand. A common start is about 7 grams to 100 ml, one quick rinse, then short steeps that lengthen as the leaf opens; it gives eight or more good cups.

notice.text: A smooth, deep cup with woody, date-like or medicinal notes, which the trade calls aged aroma.
